characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy concentrates on proving that a platform-neutral or fallback authentication model is technically viable within the Danish context. It governs the selection and execution of demonstrators, balancing security, privacy, and interoperability while avoiding production-risk. It aims to produce two credible non-production demonstrators (mobile FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback) that validate standards-based identities and interoperability with existing public-sector protocols. Key success metrics include demonstrator completion, adherence to FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect, risk/feasibility findings, and a technical posture that enables policy and procurement discussions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: By delivering concrete demonstrators, Technical Feasibility Strategy boosts credibility for Procurement Influence Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy, helping to define what platform-neutral solutions can look like in practice. It complements Coalition Building Strategy by providing tangible evidence to civil-society and privacy advocates, and supports Policy Advocacy Strategy with actionable technical findings.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Concentrating on a small set of demonstration paths may limit exploration of alternatives and increase development cost, creating tension with Coalition Building Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy by narrowing the evidence base. It could also clash with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if demonstrator results diverge from European directions.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the public and political framing of Denmark's platform-neutral fallback objective, translating technical feasibility and procurement aims into policy language and governance expectations. It seeks to influence Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, folketing digital policy committee, and other stakeholders by framing resilience, continuity of service, procurement neutrality, and supplier concentration risk as core public-interest concerns. Objectives include formal policy proposals, stakeholder matrix, and prospects for adoption of platform-neutral standards; success metrics: policy proposals submitted, formal responses from authorities, and inclusion of platform-neutral language in official documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Policy Advocacy Strategy leverages the credibility gains from Technical Feasibility Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy to push procurement language and governance expectations. It benefits from EU Standards Engagement Strategy by aligning domestic policy with European directions, and from Procurement Influence Strategy by translating policy into concrete procurement criteria.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Policy framing can become a battleground where coalition fissures, privacy debates, and procurement interests clash. It may constrain agility in procurement and risk regulatory capture by incumbents if policy is too narrowly focused. Potential friction with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if EU signals push different priorities.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy orchestrates a broad, diverse network to support platform-neutral and fallback authentication goals. It identifies and engages civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, and sympathetic policymakers. The lever aims to maximize legitimacy, weigh diverse perspectives, and accelerate consensus, producing broad backing that amplifies policy and procurement aims. Success metrics include a larger stakeholder roster, more formal commitments, and a demonstrable shift in discourse toward resilience and neutrality. Risks include misalignment between participants and decision gates, and slower progress due to competing priorities.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Coalition Building Strategy powers Policy Advocacy Strategy by delivering a broad legitimacy base, and strengthens Procurement Influence Strategy through diverse stakeholder input that informs procurement criteria. It also pairs with Technical Feasibility Strategy by validating practical, security-conscious demonstrations across different community groups.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Expanding breadth risks diluting focus and slowing decision gates, potentially delaying procurement commitments and policy deadlines. It may introduce conflicting priorities among participants, complicating alignment with Policy Advocacy Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy if voices push divergent agendas or stall consensus on platform-neutral language.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy seeks to embed platform-neutral and certified fallback authentication requirements into public-sector procurement practices, especially AltID-related documents. It translates policy and technical findings into concrete procurement criteria, while promoting supplier diversity and competition. The lever aims for immediate inclusion of platform-neutral language in procurement documents, plus systemic benefits of broader vendor participation and reduced reliance on a single technology stack. Success metrics include documented procurement language changes, measurable increases in vendor diversity, and faster scalability through compliant suppliers; key risks include gaming and misalignment with technical feasibility.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Procurement Influence Strategy directly enables Policy Advocacy Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy by aligning procurement criteria with European requirements. It also reinforces Coalition Building Strategy by delivering concrete incentives for diverse vendors to participate, and supports Technical Feasibility Strategy with procurement-aligned feedback on demonstrator viability.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Procurement pressure can risk commoditization of security, triggering rushed decisions or vendor gaming to meet short-term criteria. It may constrain creative demonstrations if cost becomes the dominant gatekeeper, potentially conflicting with Technical Feasibility Strategy. It also risks skewing Coalition Building Strategy toward procurement interests over broader public-good concerns.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy coordinates Denmark's participation in European standardization bodies to advance platform-neutral and fallback authentication within the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. It translates domestic policy and technical demonstrations into EU-aligned requirements and testable proposals, seeking early visibility and influence on eIDAS2, NSIS, and wallet interoperability. The lever aims to improve cross-border interoperability, reduce system lock-in, and create a credible European pathway for certified fallback authentication. Success metrics include inputs to EU working groups, alignment with Wallet materials, and demonstrable interoperability gains.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: EU Standards Engagement Strategy amplifies and legitimizes Procurement Influence Strategy by aligning domestic procurement criteria with European requirements. It also strengthens Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy through shared EU narratives, while enhancing Technical Feasibility Strategy by validating demonstrator results against European interoperability expectations.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: EU standards pressure can create misalignment with national procurement cycles or domestic policy timelines, risking delays. It may ignite friction with Policy Advocacy Strategy if EU signals push different priorities. It could also complicate Coalition Building Strategy if member organizations interpret EU directions variably.
